corpus.title: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of ‘all-out invasion’
corpus.signal_text:
Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of ‘all-out invasion’
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of sending troops deep into its territory and warned that it must defend itself against an “all-out invasion,” escalating a confrontation between the former allies.
Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos alleged that Eritrean forces, including mechanized units, had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray. His October 8 letter was addressed to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot and circulated to other UN Security Council members, Reuters reported Friday. The letter described the incursion as a “blatant act of aggression” and sought international support for Ethiopia’s right to self-defense.
Ethiopia’s Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Gedion briefed UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina J. Mohammed on what it called Eritrea’s “continued aggression,” demanded the immediate withdrawal of Eritrean forces and urged a “clear and principled UN response.”
In separate talks with senior UN officials, Ethiopian State Minister Berhanu Tsegaye alleged direct Eritrean military involvement “across different fronts along the border” and called for the UN to unequivocally condemn the “flagrant violations of sovereignty.”
Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel rejected Ethiopia’s accusations on Friday, calling them “audacity and duplicity in their most extreme forms.” He accused Addis Ababa of pursuing a war of aggression for more than three years, citing statements by Ethiopian leaders about acquiring sovereign access to the Red Sea and taking control of the port of Assab.
There are fears that renewed clashes between federal forces and Tigrayan fighters could plunge northern Ethiopia back into war. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which formed an alliance with six other armed groups seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government, declared a “defensive war” last month. Its forces seized airports in Mekelle, Tigray’s regional capital, and the cities of Axum and Shire, prompting Ethiopian Airlines to suspend flights to the region.
On Sunday, the government-allied Tigray Peace Force announced it had retaken Mekelle following the TPLF’s withdrawal. The TPLF said it had decided to “temporarily leave” and operate from another location while continuing military operations.

corpus.title: Ethiopian forces regain control of border city after reported Eritrean incursion
corpus.signal_text:
Ethiopian forces regain control of border city after reported Eritrean incursion
Oct 10 - Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered Adigrat, near the border with Horn of Africa neighbour Eritrea, on Saturday, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops were pushed back from the strategic city.
The incursion by Eritrean troops, which Eritrea has denied and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to all-out war along Ethiopia's northern border where the two nations have clashed before. Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes.
Three Adigrat residents told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles.
Reuters could not confirm whether the army was in control of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea. Ethiopia's military did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and city officials were not reachable on Saturday.
Ethiopia said in a letter to members of the UN Security Council this week that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside Tigray in recent days, warning that the presence of foreign forces left it with no option but to defend itself.
Eritrea has said reports of an Eritrean incursion are false and part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression.
Explosions were reported near Adigrat on Wednesday and Thursday as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city.
The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s spokesperson and Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT
Yemane said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint, accusing landlocked Ethiopia of declaring a war of aggression against his country by stating in 2023 it would acquire sovereign access to the sea.

corpus.title: Syria Studying Military Support for Saudi Arabia in Yemen War
corpus.signal_text:
Syria is cautiously considering providing military assistance to Saudi Arabia as the war against the Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen escalates, Reuters reported, citing a US official and a Syrian military official familiar with the matter. The options under discussion range from defensive support for the kingdom to deploying Syrian forces alongside Yemeni forces backed by Riyadh.
The two officials told Reuters the options include defensive assistance aimed at protecting Saudi Arabia from attacks, or deploying Syrian forces in an offensive role to help operations by Riyadh-backed Yemeni forces against the Houthis.
Reuters quoted the US official as saying Saudi Arabia asked Syria to deploy forces to join the fight against the Houthis. Riyadh is seeking military support from the United States and European and Middle Eastern countries, either to strengthen its defenses or to support offensive operations in the renewed war against the group.
Al-Sharaa Discussed the Matter in Riyadh
According to the US official, Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa discussed the possibility of Syria providing military assistance to the kingdom with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman during his public visit to Riyadh on Tuesday, along with other issues covered in the talks.
Reuters noted that footage broadcast by Syrian state media showed Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman accompanying al-Sharaa back to his plane after the visit. The agency added that Khalid bin Salman, the Saudi crown prince’s brother, oversees the Yemen file.
The Saudi government’s media office and Yemen’s information minister did not respond to Reuters’ requests for comment on the information about the talks over a possible Syrian role.
Damascus: Priority Is Domestic Issues
A Syrian diplomat, responding to a Reuters request for comment through the Syrian Foreign Ministry, said Damascus stands “firmly” with Saudi Arabia against the Houthi attacks. He stressed, however, that the Syrian government’s main priority at present is domestic issues and recovery from the effects of the war the country has been through.
The diplomat added that any Saudi request for military cooperation or an exchange of expertise would be handled exclusively through official channels and within the bilateral agreements governing relations between the two countries.

corpus.title: Tigray insurgency withers as federal forces enter Shire and resume flights to Mekelle
corpus.signal_text:
Ethiopia and Eritrea each accused the other of starting a war on Friday as an internal Ethiopian conflict threatened to escalate into a regional war.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993 and they fought a brutal border war from 1998 to 2000.
Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of backing rebels in its northern Tigray state, who launched attacks against federal forces last month.
The two countries severed diplomatic relations last week, and since then, Eritrean forces have invaded Ethiopian territory, with a foreign security source estimating it has 5,000 to 8,000 troops in Tigray.
Eritrea’s conduct is “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”, Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos wrote in a letter to diplomats.
Eritrea’s information minister, Yemane Gebremeskel, responded on X that it was facing “an unprovoked war of aggression” from Ethiopia.
Over the past week, the Ethiopian army has pushed back the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and seized their capital, Mekelle.
It has also launched drone strikes against the Eritrean troops in the region, forcing them into an apparent retreat, though a lack of access for media makes verification difficult.
Rebels lose cities
Witnesses told AFP on Friday that the rebels had lost two other cities in Tigray: Shire and Adigrat.
A Shire resident said pro-government forces had entered the city on Friday afternoon.
“People are coming out to watch the armed fighters arriving. Shops are closed. To prevent looting, residents have organised themselves in their respective neighbourhoods and are guarding their areas,” the resident said.
An aid worker in Shire said rebel fighters and the local administration abandoned the city on Wednesday, and that four people had been killed in exchanges of fire related to the looting.
Eritrean forces were seen in Adigrat in recent days before being targeted by Ethiopian drone strikes, according to a conflict monitor and witnesses.
The rebels were retreating to Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, according to a Tigrayan official from a TPLF dissident faction.
In a sign of renewed government confidence, Ethiopian Airlines said flights to the Tigrayan capital would resume from Sunday.
Kjetil Tronvoll, regional specialist at Oslo New University College, told AFP the government would likely appoint a new interim administration for the region.
He said the TPLF was “withering”, with low morale and frustration with their lead
